questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A great social student environment and nice and sweet people. It was important for me that the exchange university had place for more than one danish exchange student. It helped me feel safe and sound when I were able to share information, experiences, questions and funny stories with other students traveling from UCPH.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not easy, since UCPH had a very complicated and long process with many steps. Luckily we were four people travelling to the same university from UCPH, so we helped each other remembering and figuring out what to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got lot of assistance when arriving at University College Cork. They were so sweet and helpful, and we were assigned a student peer-buddy to help with any questions, whether it regarded housing, medical help, courses or IT-issues. The employees at UCC were also very helpful and quick to answer any emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through some of the other students going to Cork. I think they just made a Google-search and the student accommodation were through a private company called "HATCH Student accommodation". It was a very expensive place to live, but it was always clean, I felt safe and the staff were very sweet and helpful. So it was worth the money.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure that the company is real and that there are contact information on someone working there. You can try calling them to get a feeling if you can trust them or if it's a scam. Another important factor is to start looking for housing very early when you get offered an exchange. The housing get booked out so fast, and many people had to live on hotels for three months, which is both very expensive but also very lonely.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very expensive, but safety and cleanliness made it worth it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My host university sent out the catalogue via gmail, and we plugged in which courses we wanted and sent it back to them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail correspondence with the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose courses that would fit into your interests.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Since Ireland is a common law country there is a lot more focus on caselaw than at UCPH, but it is a nice twist even though you need to adjust to it at first.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching were very different and based on dialogue between students and the teacher. It was a very interesting way to learn how to make your own opinions and be critical towards the legislation in stead of just learning about their existence as you do at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Child Law in Practice
Criminology
Juvenile Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Child Law in Practice, since Connor O'Manny is a very good teacher and professor. The course is very interesting and you learn to be critical towards how the legislation in reality works in practice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My phone broke, so I had to buy a new one for 3500 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing way more expensive, but food/groceries were cheeper. Cork, Ireland were about 20% cheaper than in Copenhagen in general.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UCC has a lot of societies, clubs and events. They do a lot of work for helping the students feeling "at home", safe and included, so there is almost too many options. You just need to choose.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many different sports clubs (football, handball, boxing, kickboxing, athletics, swimming, mountaineering, dancing, singing etc.), societies (feminist society, Harry Potter society, book clubs, welcome refugees society, drama society etc.) and so much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Societies in general to meet different people, and in Cork I would especially recommend the mountaineering club to go hiking in the beautiful natures of Ireland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, travelling to near countries or cities or taking the bus or train around the city or outside the city. Ask locals what to see when visiting their city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy and also possible to do it at your own pace.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Openness, respectfulness and curiousness.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. Irish people are so sweet, funny, welcoming and easy to be around and talk to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the Irish people and community. You feel very much at home very quickly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Talk to people, try irish dancing and go to a trad-session at a pub.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Appreciate the societies and clubs, but remember to listen to your own needs as well. There are a lot to do, you could easily socialise every hour of every day, but you do not have to. Do it in your own pace and make the exchange experience as you want it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Socialising with new people and adjusting to living in a new culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling a bit homesick at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
